name: LabSpace
tagline: Build front panels, wire typed block diagrams and run them live
summary: LabSpace is a graphical instrumentation studio for desktop and the browser: design front panels, connect typed block diagrams, inspect live values and run simulated signal-processing programs. It is a working independent implementation inspired by the classic NI LabVIEW workflow, with resumable nested execution, a step-into debugger and Skia-rendered editors that share one C# codebase across native and WebAssembly hosts.

highlights.title: Paired panel and diagram
highlights.text: Every VI has a Front Panel instrument interface and a Block Diagram program. Ctrl+E switches between them and Split shows both side by side.

highlights.title: Typed dataflow wiring
highlights.text: Named terminals, single-driver inputs and output fan-out, with color-coded wires for numbers, Booleans, strings and waveforms. Incompatible types are rejected.

highlights.title: Typed structures
highlights.text: For, While, Boolean Case and embedded SubVI nodes with typed tunnels, numeric auto-indexing, conditional collection and stacked shift registers.

highlights.title: Real signal processing
highlights.text: Simulated sine, square and triangle sources feed filtering, RMS, peak-to-peak and Hann-windowed FFT kernels. Plots show real dataflow results, not decoration.

highlights.title: Step-into debugger
highlights.text: Step over or into nested execution, set breakpoints inside structure bodies, highlight execution and attach probes to named outputs.

highlights.title: Quick Drop
highlights.text: Press Ctrl+Space, search for a function or control, press Enter and click to place it on the cursor position.

highlights.title: Skia-rendered editors
highlights.text: Both editors draw with SkiaSharp through Uno's SKCanvasElement, with visible-area culling, cached wire paths and SKPicture structure previews.

highlights.title: Recovery built in
highlights.text: Browser recovery uses per-origin IndexedDB and native hosts use application data. Invalid recovery is preserved rather than silently overwritten.

Clean Up arranges nodes by dependency rank

For, While, Boolean Case and embedded SubVI connector contracts
Typed tunnels for numbers, Booleans, Unicode strings, numeric arrays and waveforms
Numeric input/output auto-indexing, conditional collection and array concatenation
Initialized and uninitialized stacked shift registers
Staged Tunnels and shift registers editor: Apply is one undoable transaction
Cached topological plans that compile only when code changes
Run, run continuously, pause and abort
Step over (F10) and nested step into (F11)
Nested breakpoints, execution highlight and cooperative cancellation
Shared node budgets bound loops to 10,000 iterations
Arithmetic, transcendentals, Boolean logic and typed Select
Unicode string transforms and numeric array transforms
Waveform construction and simulated sine, square and triangle sources
Gain/offset, moving average, RMS, peak-to-peak and FFT
Version-2 .labspace.json with source-generated serialization
Automatic migration of version-1 project files
Waveform CSV export from a selected waveform or array
Browser IndexedDB and native application-data recovery

playground.intro: The live build is the real C#/Uno WebAssembly studio with four executable example VIs, so every plot you see comes from a running dataflow graph.

tour.title: Tune a signal
tour.text: Open Signal Analysis.vi, drag Amplitude or click Frequency on the front panel, then press Ctrl+R to run again and watch the waveform, RMS and spectrum update.

tour.title: Run it continuously
tour.text: Press F6 to run continuously on the 40 ms timer, click a graph to position its value cursor, then pause or abort.

tour.title: Accumulate with shift registers
tour.text: Open Indexed Accumulator.vi and Run to get 15 and [1,3,6,10,15]. Open Tunnels and shift registers, turn off Initialized, Apply and run twice for 15 then 30.

tour.title: Quick Drop a function
tour.text: Switch to the Block Diagram with Ctrl+E, press Ctrl+Space, search for a function, press Enter and click to place it. Click an output terminal, then an input, to wire it.

tour.title: Step through execution
tour.text: Press F10 to step over top-level nodes or F11 to step into a loop body; the context-help pane shows the active frame and recent values.

tour.title: Save and export
tour.text: Press Ctrl+S to download a .labspace.json project, or select a waveform and use Export Waveform CSV.

architecture.name: Model
architecture.text: Mutable authoring models, immutable runtime values and immutable structure contracts, with no XAML dependency.

architecture.name: Engines
architecture.text: Bounded signal kernels plus a graph compiler and resumable runtime with nested activations and shared budgets.

architecture.name: Documents and editing
architecture.text: Versioned JSON persistence, host-neutral storage/recovery and a transactional editing and debugging session.

architecture.name: Rendering
architecture.text: SkiaSharp instrument, plot and typed-diagram rendering with cached wire paths and SKPicture previews.

architecture.name: Uno workbench
architecture.text: Reusable Uno canvases, palettes and inspectors composed into the complete embeddable studio.

boundaries: Not a complete, pixel-identical or binary-compatible LabVIEW replacement; the full G language is not implemented
NI .vi, .ctl and .lvproj files are not imported; older LabSpace 0.1 cannot read version-2 files
Acquisition is simulated: no NI-DAQmx, VISA, instrument drivers or physical I/O
DSP/dataflow run as managed CPU code, not WebGPU compute; scheduling is cooperative, not hard real time
Not validated for safety-critical equipment or physical/hard-real-time control
